profiles.name: German quality and Prädikat wine framework
researchNotes: Prädikat is a grape-ripeness/must-weight classification whose minimum values depend on grape variety and growing region; it is not a universal sweetness scale.
Quality and Prädikat wines must come entirely from one of the 13 German Anbaugebiete and pass quality assessment.

profiles.name: Mosel

terroir.steepSlopeShare: about half of vineyard area is on steep or terraced sites above 30 degrees

styleNotes: Riesling is the defining variety and is strongly associated with steep river-valley sites
Elbling remains an important historic specialty of the southern Mosel

profiles.name: Rheingau

terroir.geography: vineyards extend along the right bank of the Rhine; the Rhine bend creates an important mesoclimate

researchNotes: This pass records current regional planting/geographic context. Exact PDO village/site and modern origin-tier rules require a legal-specification pass.

profiles.name: Pfalz
researchNotes: Pfalz is the second-largest German growing region in the 2025 DWI snapshot and the largest German red-wine area by planted hectares in that snapshot.
Exact PDO/Grosslage/Einzellage legal hierarchy needs separate extraction.

profiles.name: Rheinhessen

terroir.climate: low rainfall, warm summers and mild winters, protected by uplands to the west

researchNotes: Current planting statistics are snapshot data and must be year-labelled rather than treated as timeless regional rules.

profiles.name: Ahr

terroir.geography: steep vineyards above the Ahr river in northern Rheinland-Pfalz

researchNotes: Ahr's red-wine identity is strong, but generation should not assume every Ahr wine is Pinot-derived without a legal/product specification.

profiles.name: Santorini
products: sweet fortified wine from dried grapes

terroir.phylloxera: sandy low-clay soils preserved self-rooted vines
terroir.climate: dry, windy island climate with strong northerly Meltemi

styleNotes: dry Assyrtiko is high-acid, structured and saline/mineral
Vinsanto combines concentrated sweetness with unusually high acidity and oxidative ageing complexity

profiles.name: Nemea
products: sweet red wine from dried grapes

terroir.climate: Mediterranean with substantial mesoclimate variation by altitude

styleNotes: Agiorgitiko can range from fresh fruit-driven reds to structured ageworthy wines
higher-altitude variation can materially change ripening and style

profiles.name: Naoussa

terroir.geography: mainly south-eastern slopes of Mount Vermio

styleNotes: typically pale in color with high acidity and high tannin
traditional long-maceration/wood-aged styles can be austere young and highly ageworthy
modern styles emphasize fruit while retaining structural tannin

profiles.name: Mantinia

terroir.climate: cool Mediterranean with continental influence; late ripening, with spring frost and hail risks

styleNotes: floral, rose-like and citrus aromas with high acidity
still and sparkling expressions are both legal PDO styles

profiles.name: Tokaj

productionRules.aszuBerrySelection: botrytised, shrivelled berries picked separately by hand
productionRules.aszuEarliestRelease: 1 January of the third year after harvest
productionRules.protectedOriginBottling: Tokaj PDO wines must be bottled within the product-specification area

terroir.climate: warm, dry continental overall with local autumn humidity important for noble rot
terroir.geology: highly varied, with substantial volcanic bedrock and soils

styleNotes: Furmint supplies marked acidity and strong botrytis aptitude
Hárslevelű is generally softer and more aromatic
Sárgamuskotály is the most overtly aromatic of the main varieties
Aszú depends on noble rot and individual berry selection
researchNotes: The current regional source lists six permitted varieties and reports Furmint as dominant. Planting percentages are snapshot values and should remain date-stamped if imported.

profiles.name: United States federal wine origin, variety and vintage framework

productionRules.avaFinishRequirement: wine must be fully finished, subject to limited cellar-treatment/blending exceptions, in the state or one of the states containing the AVA

researchNotes: AVA identity is a geographic-origin system; an AVA does not itself impose an authorized-grape list.
A varietal designation requires an appellation of origin, and the qualifying named-variety proportion must come from that labeled appellation.

profiles.name: Napa Valley
researchNotes: Legal AVA identity and federal label thresholds are established. Sub-AVA, climate, soil, and cultivar distributions require dedicated petition/official regional research before the game assigns them as universal Napa traits.

profiles.name: Willamette Valley
researchNotes: The AVA predates its nested modern sub-AVAs. Nested geography should be represented only from the TTB hierarchy rather than inferred from marketing usage.

profiles.name: Finger Lakes
researchNotes: TTB explicitly lists Cayuga Lake and Seneca Lake as AVAs contained within Finger Lakes.

profiles.name: Ontario VQA framework

productionRules.productionLocation: VQA wine is fermented, processed, blended, finished and bottled in Ontario

researchNotes: Ontario has a formal distinction between provincial, viticultural-area, sub-appellation and vineyard origin claims.
Current rules include protected production/style terms in addition to geography.

profiles.name: Niagara Peninsula
researchNotes: Sub-appellation origin requirements are more specific and are not automatically inherited as the same 85% rule. Each named sub-appellation should be researched against the current regulation before generation uses it.

profiles.name: Beamsville Bench
researchNotes: Protected sub-appellation identity is current. Exact current boundary and origin-percentage treatment will be extracted separately from the consolidated regulation rather than copied from an older amendment.

profiles.name: Four Mile Creek
researchNotes: Protected current term. A dedicated sub-appellation pass will add boundary, soils, mesoclimate and exact current origin rule.

profiles.name: British Columbia VQA framework
profiles.legalClass: BC VQA / Wines of Marked Quality Regulation
researchNotes: British Columbia amended the named-GI certification threshold from 95% to 85% effective in 2025. Historical game vintages must not retroactively use the new rule.
All Vitis vinifera varieties are permitted for BC VQA plus a regulated list of interspecific varieties.

profiles.name: Okanagan Valley
researchNotes: The 2025 rule change is version-sensitive; older vintages and label regimes may have used a 95% GI threshold.
Sub-GIs are legally separate origin units and should not be treated as marketing nicknames.

profiles.name: Naramata Bench
researchNotes: Boundary identity is regulated. A separate petition/terroir pass is required before grape or style expectations are encoded.

profiles.name: Golden Mile Bench
researchNotes: Protected sub-GI identity only in this pass; no unsourced cultivar stereotypes are added.

profiles.name: Okanagan Falls
researchNotes: Protected sub-GI identity only in this pass; physical-environment evidence will be added from the official application/decision material.

profiles.name: Australian wine GI, variety and vintage blending framework
profiles.legalClass: Wine Australia Act / Regulations / Label Integrity Program
researchNotes: Australian GI hierarchy describes geographic scale, not a quality ranking.
Registered GI identity is protected and origin claims are audited through the Label Integrity Program.

profiles.name: Margaret River
researchNotes: The legal textual boundary, not a stylized map, is the definitive GI definition. Variety/style enrichment will be added separately.

profiles.name: Coonawarra
researchNotes: Legal boundary and GI hierarchy are sourced; cultivar and terra rossa style assumptions are deliberately deferred to a dedicated official regional pass.

profiles.name: McLaren Vale
researchNotes: Legal GI identity and hierarchy verified. Detailed mesoclimate, geology and planting distributions remain a separate research unit.

profiles.name: Hunter Valley
researchNotes: Hunter Valley is a registered GI. Nested Hunter/Pokolbin/Upper Hunter relationships need a separate hierarchy normalization pass before they are generated.

profiles.name: Yarra Valley
researchNotes: Legal GI identity and placement within Port Phillip verified; detailed variety/style modeling awaits official regional evidence.

profiles.name: Clare Valley
researchNotes: Legal GI identity and hierarchy verified. Riesling/Shiraz expectations are not added as hard generation rules in this pass.

profiles.name: Tasmania
researchNotes: Tasmania is a registered state-level GI. Subregional terms should not be promoted to registered GI status without checking the Wine Australia register.
